quick: IR: 5 mcg SC BID, up to 10 mcg BID; ER: 2 mg SC weekly
IR: within 60 min before two main meals; ER: any time, no meal tie
Avoid; insufficient data, use only if clearly needed
Avoid if CrCl < 30 (IR) / eGFR < 45 (ER); caution moderate
Glucose/HbA1c, renal function, signs of pancreatitis
summary: Exenatide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist for type 2 diabetes, available as an immediate-release injection (5-10 mcg twice daily before meals) and an extended-release formulation (2 mg subcutaneously once weekly). It enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses inappropriate glucagon, slows gastric emptying and promotes satiety. Important safety concerns are acute pancreatitis and, for the extended-release product, a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors; it should be avoided in severe renal impairment.
indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

dosage.n: Within 60 minutes before the two main meals at least 6 h apart

dosage.d: Increase to 10 mcg twice daily after 1 month if needed

dosage.n: Any time of day, with or without meals; rotate sites

dosage.d: Use with caution; titrate IR slowly from 5 to 10 mcg

dosage.c: Severe renal impairment / ESRD (CrCl < 30 IR; eGFR < 45 ER)

admin: Inject subcutaneously into the thigh, abdomen or upper arm; rotate sites
IR: give within 60 minutes before the morning and evening meals - never after a meal
ER: reconstitute/prepare per device instructions and inject immediately; give the same day each week
Do not give intravenously or intramuscularly
Administer other oral drugs needing rapid absorption (e.g. some antibiotics, contraceptives) at least 1 hour before exenatide due to delayed gastric emptying
moa: Exenatide is an incretin mimetic that binds and activates the GLP-1 receptor. It augments glucose-dependent insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells, suppresses inappropriately elevated glucagon secretion, slows gastric emptying, and increases satiety. These actions lower postprandial and fasting glucose with a low intrinsic risk of hypoglycemia unless combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea.

absolute: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (ER formulation)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (ER formulation)
Prior serious hypersensitivity to exenatide or product components
relative: Concurrent sulfonylurea or insulin (hypoglycemia risk - reduce their dose)
monitor: Patients with thyroid nodules or elevated calcitonin (ER)

preg: There are insufficient data on exenatide in pregnancy; it is generally avoided, and during pregnancy insulin is preferred for glycemic control. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether exenatide is excreted in human milk; because of potential effects on the infant, use with caution or avoid during breastfeeding.
renal: Do not use immediate-release exenatide when creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min, and do not use the extended-release product when eGFR is below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. Use with caution in moderate impairment and titrate slowly; avoid in dialysis. Rare reports of acute kidney injury, sometimes related to dehydration from nausea/vomiting.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is recommended in hepatic impairment, as exenatide is cleared mainly by the kidneys.

major: Sulfonylureas - markedly increased hypoglycemia risk; reduce sulfonylurea dose
Insulin - increased hypoglycemia risk; reduce insulin and do not mix in the same syringe
moderate: Oral medications requiring rapid GI absorption (some antibiotics, oral contraceptives, acetaminophen) - delayed gastric emptying lowers/slows absorption; dose at least 1 h before exenatide
Warfarin - rare INR elevation/bleeding reports; monitor INR
minor: Drugs with narrow therapeutic index taken orally - timing adjustments advised
interactions.food: IR must be given before meals; food timing is integral to dosing. No specific food to avoid otherwise.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol - increases hypoglycemia risk and may contribute to pancreatitis.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum calcitonin (ER); pancreatitis presents with elevated amylase/lipase.

serious: Acute kidney injury / worsening renal function
rare: Thyroid C-cell tumors / medullary thyroid carcinoma (boxed warning for ER, based on rodent data)
emergency: Acute pancreatitis (severe persistent abdominal pain radiating to back)

monitoring: Blood glucose and HbA1c for glycemic response
Renal function, particularly with GI losses or in moderate impairment
Signs and symptoms of pancreatitis (persistent severe abdominal pain)
Body weight; thyroid symptoms/neck mass for the ER formulation
Hypoglycemia when combined with sulfonylurea or insulin
counsel: Immediate-release: inject within an hour before your two main meals; never after eating
Extended-release: inject once a week on the same day; small painless lumps at the site can occur
Stop the drug and seek urgent care for severe, persistent abdominal pain that may spread to the back (pancreatitis)
Report a neck lump, hoarseness or trouble swallowing (ER formulation); know the signs of low blood sugar if you also take a sulfonylurea or insulin
pk: IR lowers postprandial glucose within ~30-60 min
IR Tmax ~2.1 h; ER reaches steady state over 6-7 weeks
IR ~2.4 h; ER effective half-life ~2 weeks (microsphere release)
IR ~ per meal; ER sustained for 1 week
Refrigerate 2-8 C; IR pen may be kept at room temp <= 25 C after first use per label
pearls: Boxed warning (extended-release): risk of thyroid C-cell tumors - contraindicated with personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2
Acute pancreatitis can occur - discontinue promptly and do not restart if pancreatitis is confirmed
Glucose-dependent action means low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk; the danger comes from added sulfonylureas or insulin (reduce their dose)
Slowed gastric emptying can delay absorption of other oral drugs - separate timing for narrow-margin agents
missed: Immediate-release: if a pre-meal dose is missed, skip it and resume at the next scheduled meal - do not give after eating or double up. Extended-release: give a missed weekly dose as soon as possible if the next regularly scheduled dose is at least 3 days (72 hours) away; otherwise skip it and resume the usual day.
overdose: Overdose may cause severe nausea, vomiting and rapidly falling blood glucose. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, treat hypoglycemia, and manage fluid/electrolyte losses and any pancreatitis.
